statement: Let G∗ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group satisfying the following conditions. (i) G∗ is locally indicable, coherent, of type F, and has integral cohomological dimension at most two. (ii) G∗ has a division ring D(G∗) satisfying the subgroup-field hypotheses, and the chains of a finite classifying space become acyclic over D(G∗). (iii) There is a finite malnormal family {Dj} of quasiconvex hyperbolic virtually compact special subgroups such that arbitrarily deep peripheral fillings G∗ −→ Q∗ are hyperbolic and virtually compact special, and their inherited peripheral images are hyperbolic and virtually compact special. In (iii), arbitrarily deep means that the peripheral kernels can avoid any prescribed finite subset of S j(Dj \ {1}); the inherited peripheral structure is the one furnished by relative Dehn filling. Then a finite-index subgroup of G∗ is an extension of a finite-rank free group by Z. Consequently G∗ is virtually compact special.
